items_missed: No agenda statement or explicit "Sound good?" confirmation before diving into questions
Did not ask about walk distance / narrow hallways or packing service needs during the probe

Skipped pricing entirely on the call — no hourly rate, no what's-included list, no disassembly/reassembly mention, no no-hidden-fees pitch; pivoted straight to "I'll email it over" because of his own upcoming conference call
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned
On-Time Guarantee (discounting if the window is missed) never mentioned, even though the customer raised punctuality as her top concern
Clock explanation (2.5 hr minimum, 15-min prorated increments, on-site start) never given
No verbal estimate, typical time range, or mover/truck count given on the call — deferred entirely to a follow-up email
Save Your Ass prep speech (consolidation tips, "take a carload", shorter move = lower bill) entirely absent
Never explicitly said no deposit is required
Did not attempt to lock in the tomorrow 9:00-9:30 slot on the call — customer had to propose calling back herself
Did not ask "any other questions before I let you go?" or give hours/how to reach the office before ending the call
Customer's name ("Markeisha") used only once in the entire call, not the 3+ target
No empathy acknowledgment when the customer disclosed the move was prompted by her father's passing — rep responded with "Okay... I see... gotcha, gotcha" and moved on
top_strength: Jess methodically worked through the storage-unit logistics (zip codes, unit size and fullness, second-floor elevator access, driveway grade, specialty items) and still found a next-day appointment for a last-minute request.
coaching_note: Jess cut the pricing, clock, estimate, and Save Your Ass sections entirely because his own conference call was starting, pushing all of it into a follow-up email instead of walking the customer through it live — he should protect enough time on last-minute-request calls to at least verbally cover pricing and the differentiators before handing off to email.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and got some warmth in ("wonderful to meet you here"), but speech is rambly/unfocused in places and he missed an obvious empathy moment when the customer mentioned her father's passing.
